Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and agreed next steps so we have a single place to track items for your security review:

2) What we covered on the call:
- Redwood Private runs a customer-dedicated control plane with optional customer-managed VPC peering or private link.
- Model inference happens inside the VPC; no customer data is sent to shared pools unless you opt into hosted variants.
- You can bring your own KMS, and audit logs can be routed to your S3 buckets.

3) Attachments: a first-draft VPC diagram (acme_vpc_diagram.pdf) and our dataflow guidance doc (redwood-dataflow-guidance.pdf).

- Redwood to produce a short memo on PII handling + retention defaults and how to configure retention windows for logs (by 2026-05-14).
- Schedule a technical session with your infra/security + our infra engineer to validate the diagram and discuss air-gapped on-prem options (proposed: Tue 2026-05-12 or Wed 2026-05-13) 

John, which works best?

John 

Thanks, great questions. Answers at a high level below; we can expand in the technical session.

1) PII and storage
- For Redwood Private (VPC), inference happens inside customer-managed VPCs. By default, no customer request/response payloads are persisted in any Redwood shared service. You can configure the runtime to disable persistent prompt/response logging entirely.
- KV cache or persistent caches are only used if you enable them; they can be configured to use customer-provided S3 (in your account) or ephemeral encrypted disk within the VPC. We support customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-KMS).

2) Logging and retention
- Retention is configurable per-log-type. Typical default: request traces (7 days), aggregated telemetry (90 days). For customers with compliance needs we offer policy-based retention with exact windows you specify; we will document the retention APIs in the follow-up memo.

3) Egress and DNS
- Control-plane callbacks: with Redwood Private, control-plane traffic can be optionally restricted to a private control-plane endpoint over AWS PrivateLink or VPC peering. Outbound calls from inference nodes are only for model artifact pulls (initial bootstrap) and optional telemetry (which you can disable).
- For on-prem/air-gapped installs: the package can be deployed with zero outbound internet access. In that configuration we provide an offline license bundle and local-only model artifacts; no periodic callbacks are required unless you opt into telemetry/updates.

4) On-prem package specifics
- Includes the runtime binaries, a local model store, and an ops-runbook for offline upgrades. We support a fully air-gapped deployment model; the tradeoffs are that you are responsible for model updates and offline key management (we provide guidance and tooling for that).

Attachments included here: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (SOC 2 controls mapping), and the earlier VPC diagram.
